Q: Extract data from a gsmarena page using scrapy A:

There isn’t any official public API for GSMArena or DXOMark.

Most developers either scrape the data manually or rely on incomplete third-party APIs that only provide basic specifications.

If you need a more complete solution (including DXOMark scores and camera samples), I built a REST API that combines both GSMArena and DXOMark data.

It provides:

  • Full phone specifications

  • DXOMark scores with breakdown

  • Camera samples categorized

  • Review data

Example:
GET /phone?name=samsung galaxy s25 ultra

GitHub: https://github.com/Sanjeevu-Tarun/gsmarena-dxomark-mobile-specs-api

It’s free, serverless, and doesn’t require an API key.

Q: How to avoid repeatedly passing a string slice to helper method without adding lifetime? A:

Sure it adds some overhead and if you're in the hot path for your application that may matter. But the most valuable resource is developer time, so unless and until profiling shows that ref-counting overhead slows down your application significantly, you're much better off going the easy route and spending your time in some more profitable tasks (like optimizing the places that really matter).

Q: When to prefer application code for syncing denormalized columns over a trigger? A:

There are potential reasons to prefer application code for syncing. The example case is a normalized Votes table, synced with an aggregated count in the Posts table.

  • Some part of calculating values for the sync is slow, and you don't want to bear that cost when every vote is cast. By deferring it, the request to cast a vote is a little bit faster. In the case of aggregation, it might require scanning an unbounded number of rows from the Votes table.

  • Race conditions. If multiple votes are cast concurrently in different sessions, each calculates what they think is the sum, but they don't include the other uncommitted sessions. Thus they all update the Posts table with an inaccurate value. The recommended way to avoid this if the sync is part of the same transaction that casts the vote is to make all the sessions wait on a single lock. This may create a performance bottleneck, depending on how often votes are cast concurrently.

  • The programmers don't want to use triggers. Using triggers may complicate use of their data access layer or ORM. It couples them to a specific brand of SQL database, since trigger languages are unique to each brand. Or they just don't like testing or debugging systems that have side-effects like triggers.

There could be other reasons besides these that are off the top of my head. None of these are insurmountable problems, but they might just be enough of a pain that a developer chooses to avoid them.

I don't have insight specifically into why the developers of SO avoid triggers (in fact, I don't know that that's true, I'm just taking your word for it for the sake of argument).

Q: Get Alt Text of image that's inside a cell A:

If the image is in cell A1, you can use one of the following expressions:

WorksheetFunction.ValueToText(Range("A1"))
WorksheetFunction.Text(Range("A1"),"General")

or simply:

Range("A1").Formula

Q: C++ sizeof std::vector A:

Introducing type aliases (as typedefs do) does not require any storage in each std::vector object.

Only [non-static] data members require that.

Next time, please post such a question as a "normal" (newly AKA Troubleshooting/Debugging) question rather than an open-ended "advice" one (since it has a clear answer which is not opinion based).
